name: Tiskel

anatomy.part: upper-right corner of the box body, where the top cell rises from the frame (the bright heart of the kite)
upper-left corner of the box body
lower corner of the box, where the tail ribbon is knotted on
lower-left corner of the box, rounded
bridle knot, the thin line hanging off the left side of the box
peak of the upper cell, the raised top corner of the kite
lower-right corner of the upper cell, where the cell closes back onto the box
knot in the tail, where the thick ribbon bends into the long trailing tail
tip of the trailing tail, the last ribbon in the water-light

myth: A girl of the Holm house went down to the shingle with her brother's box-kite, new, bone-framed and bright with sailcloth. The wind took it out of her fists and she ran after it into the tide. Tavo laughed, as he does, and would not give it back. Kael cast his net all that night for her and hauled up only weed. Now in spring the family climbs the cliff with a second box-kite they made to replace the first, and they fly it out over the water where she went under. Hesk winds the string and keeps count of the years. The kite goes up into the Leeward road and sits there in the cold, a box with a tail, and the mother says the girl's hand is on the line, though no one has ever seen it. When the wind drops they reel it in, wet at the corners, and they are glad to have it back. Then they send it up again, because the sky has not yet said no.
verse:
Spring wind on the cliff,
the box climbs over the salt,
her hand on the line.
